sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ rājā sa mahātmā hy atīva; svair dauhitrais tārito 'mitrasāhaḥ tyaktvā mahīṃ paramodārakarmā; svargaṃ gataḥ karmabhir vyāpya pṛthvīm
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus that great-souled king Yayāti, the destroyer of foes, was ferried across by his own grandsons. Having abandoned the earth, he whose deeds were supremely noble ascended to heaven, his karmas pervading the whole world.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi pūror vaṃśakarān nṛpān yadvīryā yādṛśāś caiva yāvanto yatparākramāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: Venerable one, I wish to hear about the kings who continued the line of Pūru — what valor they possessed, what manner of men they were, how many there were, and what their prowess.

sanskrit: na hy asmiñ śīlahīno vā nirvīryo vā narādhipaḥ prajāvirahito vāpi bhūtapūrvaḥ kadā cana
english: For in this lineage there has never at any time been a king who was lacking in good character, or lacking in valor, or without progeny.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ prathitavṛttānāṃ rājñāṃ vijñānaśālinām caritaṃ śrotum icchāmi vistareṇa tapodhana
english: O wealth of austerity, I wish to hear in detail the deeds of those kings whose conduct was celebrated and who were endowed with discernment.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi pūror vaṃśadharān vīrāñ śakrapratimatejasaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Well then, I shall tell you what you ask of me — the heroic upholders of Pūru's lineage, whose splendor rivaled that of Indra.

sanskrit: pravīreśvararaudrāśvās trayaḥ putrā mahārathāḥ pūroḥ pauṣṭyām ajāyanta pravīras tatra vaṃśakṛt
english: Pravīra, Īśvara, and Raudrāśva — three great chariot-warriors — were born to Pūru by Pauṣṭī; of them, Pravīra continued the line.

sanskrit: manasyur abhavat tasmāc chūraḥ śyenīsutaḥ prabhuḥ pṛthivyāś caturantāyā goptā rājīvalocanaḥ
english: From him was born Manasyu, valiant son of Śyenī, a lord and protector of the earth to its four horizons, with eyes like lotus petals.

sanskrit: subhrūḥ saṃhanano vāgmī sauvīrītanayās trayaḥ manasyor abhavan putrāḥ śūrāḥ sarve mahārathāḥ
english: Subhrū, Saṃhana, and Vāgmī — three sons of Sauvīrī — were born to Manasyu; all were brave great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: raudrāśvasya maheṣvāsā daśāpsarasi sūnavaḥ yajvāno jajñire śūrāḥ prajāvanto bahuśrutāḥ sarve sarvāstravidvāṃsaḥ sarve dharmaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Raudrāśva's ten sons by an apsarā were great archers who performed sacrifices, born as brave men with abundant progeny and great learning; all were knowledgeable in every weapon, all were devoted to dharma.

sanskrit: ṛcepur atha kakṣepuḥ kṛkaṇepuś ca vīryavān sthaṇḍilepur vanepuś ca sthalepuś ca mahārathaḥ
english: They were Ṛcepu, Kakṣepu, the valiant Kṛkaṇepu, Sthaṇḍilepu, Vanepu, and Sthalepuṣa the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: tejepur balavān dhīmān satyepuś cendravikramaḥ dharmepuḥ saṃnatepuś ca daśamo devavikramaḥ anādhṛṣṭisutās tāta rājasūyāśvamedhinaḥ
english: Tejepu the powerful and wise, Satyepu of Indra-like valor, Dharmepu, Saṃnatepu — the tenth with the prowess of a god — these sons of Anādhṛṣṭi, dear one, all performed the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha sacrifices.

sanskrit: matināras tato rājā vidvāṃś carceputo 'bhavat matinārasutā rājaṃś catvāro 'mitavikramāḥ taṃsur mahān atiratho druhyuś cāpratimadyutiḥ
english: After them king Matināra, learned son of Carcepu, was born; O king, Matināra's four sons were of boundless valor: the great Taṃsu, a warrior surpassing even chariot-fighters, and Druhyu of unrivaled brilliance.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ taṃsur mahāvīryaḥ pauravaṃ vaṃśam udvahan ājahāra yaśo dīptaṃ jigāya ca vasuṃdharām
english: Of them, Taṃsu of great valor, bearing the Paurava lineage onward, won blazing glory and conquered the earth.

sanskrit: ilinaṃ tu sutaṃ taṃsur janayām āsa vīryavān so 'pi kṛtsnām imāṃ bhūmiṃ vijigye jayatāṃ varaḥ
english: The valiant Taṃsu fathered a son named Ilina, and he too conquered this entire earth — foremost among conquerors.

sanskrit: rathaṃtaryāṃ sutān pañca pañcabhūtopamāṃs tataḥ ilino janayām āsa duḥṣantaprabhṛtīn nṛpa
english: O king, Ilina then fathered five sons on Rathaṃtarī — sons comparable to the five elements — headed by Duḥṣanta.

sanskrit: duḥṣantaṃ śūrabhīmau ca prapūrvaṃ vasum eva ca teṣāṃ jyeṣṭho 'bhavad rājā duḥṣanto janamejaya
english: They were Duḥṣanta, Śūra, Bhīma, Prapūrva, and Vasu; of them the eldest became king — Duḥṣanta, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: duḥṣantād bharato jajñe vidvāñ śākuntalo nṛpaḥ tasmād bharatavaṃśasya vipratasthe mahad yaśaḥ
english: From Duḥṣanta was born Bharata, the wise king son of Śakuntalā; from him the great glory of the Bharata lineage spread wide.

sanskrit: bharatas tisṛṣu strīṣu nava putrān ajījanat nābhyanandanta tān rājā nānurūpā mamety uta
english: Bharata fathered nine sons on three wives, but the king did not rejoice in them, saying, "They do not resemble me."

sanskrit: tato mahadbhiḥ kratubhir ījāno bharatas tadā lebhe putraṃ bharadvājād bhumanyuṃ nāma bhārata
english: Then Bharata, who had performed great sacrifices, obtained through Bharadvāja a son named Bhumanyu, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: tataḥ putriṇam ātmānaṃ jñātvā pauravanandanaḥ bhumanyuṃ bharataśreṣṭha yauvarājye 'bhyaṣecayat
english: Then, knowing himself to be blessed with a son, the delight of the Pauravas consecrated Bhumanyu as crown prince, O best of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tatas tasya mahīndrasya vitathaḥ putrako 'bhavat tataḥ sa vitatho nāma bhumanyor abhavat sutaḥ
english: Then for that great lord of the earth a son named Vitatha was born; thus Vitatha was the son of Bhumanyu.

sanskrit: suhotraś ca suhotā ca suhaviḥ suyajus tathā puṣkariṇyām ṛcīkasya bhumanyor abhavan sutāḥ
english: Suhotra, Suhotā, Suhavi, and Suyaju — sons of Ṛcīka's daughter Puṣkariṇī — were born to Bhumanyu.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ jyeṣṭhaḥ suhotras tu rājyam āpa mahīkṣitām rājasūyāśvamedhādyaiḥ so 'yajad bahubhiḥ savaiḥ
english: Of them the eldest, Suhotra, obtained sovereignty over kings of the earth; he performed many sacrifices including the Rājasūya and Aśvamedha.

sanskrit: suhotraḥ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ bubhuje sāgarāmbarām pūrṇāṃ hastigavāśvasya bahuratnasamākulām
english: Suhotra enjoyed all the earth girdled by the ocean, full of elephants, cattle, and horses, and teeming with many treasures.

sanskrit: mamajjeva mahī tasya bhūribhārāvapīḍitā hastyaśvarathasaṃpūrṇā manuṣyakalilā bhṛśam
english: The earth seemed to sink under his enormous weight, overflowing with elephants, horses, and chariots, and exceedingly crowded with people.

sanskrit: suhotre rājani tadā dharmataḥ śāsati prajāḥ caityayūpāṅkitā cāsīd bhūmiḥ śatasahasraśaḥ pravṛddhajanasasyā ca sahadevā vyarocata
english: While king Suhotra ruled his subjects according to dharma, the earth was marked with hundreds of thousands of sacrificial stakes and altars; teeming with flourishing people and grain, it shone together with the gods.

sanskrit: aikṣvākī janayām āsa suhotrāt pṛthivīpateḥ ajamīḍhaṃ sumīḍhaṃ ca purumīḍhaṃ ca bhārata
english: O Bhārata, Aikṣvākī bore to Suhotra, lord of the earth, three sons: Ajamīḍha, Sumīḍha, and Purumīḍha.

sanskrit: ajamīḍho varas teṣāṃ tasmin vaṃśaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ ṣaṭ putrān so 'py ajanayat tisṛṣu strīṣu bhārata
english: Ajamīḍha was the best of them; in him the lineage was established. He in turn fathered six sons on three wives, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ṛkṣaṃ dhūminy atho nīlī duḥṣantaparameṣṭhinau keśiny ajanayaj jahnum ubhau ca janarūpiṇau
english: Dhūminī bore Ṛkṣa; Nīlī bore Duḥṣanta and Parameṣṭhin; Keśinī bore Jahnu and both called Janarūpiṇau.

sanskrit: tatheme sarvapāñcālā duḥṣantaparameṣṭhinoḥ anvayāḥ kuśikā rājañ jahnor amitatejasaḥ
english: Thus all the Pāñcālas are descendants of Duḥṣanta and Parameṣṭhin, O king, and the Kuśikas are descendants of Jahnu of boundless splendor.

sanskrit: janarūpiṇayor jyeṣṭham ṛkṣam āhur janādhipam ṛkṣāt saṃvaraṇo jajñe rājan vaṃśakaras tava
english: Of the two Janarūpiṇas, the elder Ṛkṣa is called the lord of the people; from Ṛkṣa was born Saṃvaraṇa, O king, the one who continued your lineage.

sanskrit: ārkṣe saṃvaraṇe rājan praśāsati vasuṃdharām saṃkṣayaḥ sumahān āsīt prajānām iti śuśrumaḥ
english: When Saṃvaraṇa son of Ṛkṣa, O king, was ruling the earth, there came about a very great destruction of the people — so we have heard.

sanskrit: vyaśīryata tato rāṣṭraṃ kṣayair nānāvidhais tathā kṣunmṛtyubhyām anāvṛṣṭyā vyādhibhiś ca samāhatam abhyaghnan bhāratāṃś caiva sapatnānāṃ balāni ca
english: The kingdom then broke apart through various calamities — struck by famine, death, drought, and disease — and the armies of their enemies assailed the Bharatas as well.

sanskrit: cālayan vasudhāṃ caiva balena caturaṅgiṇā abhyayāt taṃ ca pāñcālyo vijitya tarasā mahīm akṣauhiṇībhir daśabhiḥ sa enaṃ samare 'jayat
english: Shaking the very earth with his fourfold army, the Pāñcāla king came against him; having swiftly conquered the land, he defeated Saṃvaraṇa in battle with ten akṣauhiṇī armies.

sanskrit: tataḥ sadāraḥ sāmātyaḥ saputraḥ sasuhṛjjanaḥ rājā saṃvaraṇas tasmāt palāyata mahābhayāt
english: Then king Saṃvaraṇa, together with his wives, ministers, sons, and friends, fled from there in great fear.

sanskrit: sindhor nadasya mahato nikuñje nyavasat tadā nadīviṣayaparyante parvatasya samīpataḥ tatrāvasan bahūn kālān bhāratā durgamāśritāḥ
english: He then dwelt in a thicket on the bank of the great river Sindhu, at the edge of the river region near the mountains; the Bharatas lived there for a long time, having taken refuge in that difficult terrain.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ nivasatāṃ tatra sahasraṃ parivatsarān athābhyagacchad bharatān vasiṣṭho bhagavān ṛṣiḥ
english: After they had lived there for a thousand years, the venerable sage Vasiṣṭha came to the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tam āgataṃ prayatnena pratyudgamyābhivādya ca arghyam abhyāharaṃs tasmai te sarve bhāratās tadā nivedya sarvam ṛṣaye satkāreṇa suvarcase
english: Going forth to meet him with great care and paying him homage, all the Bharatas then brought him the guest-offering of arghya, and with due reverence reported everything to the resplendent sage.

sanskrit: taṃ samām aṣṭamīm uṣṭaṃ rājā vavre svayaṃ tadā purohito bhavān no 'stu rājyāya prayatāmahe om ity evaṃ vasiṣṭho 'pi bhāratān pratyapadyata
english: Having stayed with them for eight years, the king himself then requested him: "Be our purohita — we strive for the kingdom." "So be it" — with this, Vasiṣṭha agreed and accepted the Bharatas.

sanskrit: athābhyaṣiñcat sāmrājye sarvakṣatrasya pauravam viṣāṇabhūtaṃ sarvasyāṃ pṛthivyām iti naḥ śrutam
english: Then he consecrated the Paurava king to imperial sovereignty over all the kṣatriyas, as the foremost of all on earth — so we have heard.

sanskrit: bharatādhyuṣitaṃ pūrvaṃ so 'dhyatiṣṭhat purottamam punar balibhṛtaś caiva cakre sarvamahīkṣitaḥ
english: He occupied that best of cities previously held by the Bharatas, and made all kings of the earth his tribute-bearers once more.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pṛthivīṃ prāpya punar īje mahābalaḥ ājamīḍho mahāyajñair bahubhir bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ
english: Then, having regained the earth, that mighty descendant of Ajamīḍha performed many great sacrifices with lavish fees.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃvaraṇāt saurī suṣuve tapatī kurum rājatve taṃ prajāḥ sarvā dharmajña iti vavrire
english: Then Tapatī, daughter of the Sun, bore to Saṃvaraṇa a son named Kuru; all the subjects chose him as their king, calling him "the knower of dharma."

sanskrit: tasya nāmnābhivikhyātaṃ pṛthivyāṃ kurujāṅgalam kurukṣetraṃ sa tapasā puṇyaṃ cakre mahātapāḥ
english: By his name the Kurujāṅgala region on earth became celebrated; the great ascetic made Kurukṣetra sacred through his austerities.

sanskrit: aśvavantam abhiṣvantaṃ tathā citrarathaṃ munim janamejayaṃ ca vikhyātaṃ putrāṃś cāsyānuśuśrumaḥ pañcaitān vāhinī putrān vyajāyata manasvinī
english: We have heard that his sons were Aśvavanta, Abhiṣvanta, Citraratha the sage, and the renowned Janamejaya; a noble woman bore these five sons born of the army.

sanskrit: abhiṣvataḥ parikṣit tu śabalāśvaś ca vīryavān abhirājo virājaś ca śalmalaś ca mahābalaḥ
english: From Abhiṣvata came Parikṣit; also born were the valiant Śabalāśva, Abhirāja, Virāja, and the mighty Śalmala.

sanskrit: uccaiḥśravā bhadrakāro jitāriś cāṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ eteṣām anvavāye tu khyātās te karmajair guṇaiḥ
english: Uccaiḥśravā, Bhadrakāra, and Jitāri the eighth — in the lineage of these men, their descendants became famous for virtues born of their deeds.

sanskrit: janamejayādayaḥ sapta tathaivānye mahābalāḥ parikṣito 'bhavan putrāḥ sarve dharmārthakovidāḥ
english: Janamejaya and six others, and likewise other mighty sons of Parikṣit — seven in all — were all skilled in dharma and artha.

sanskrit: kakṣasenograsenau ca citrasenaś ca vīryavān indrasenaḥ suṣeṇaś ca bhīmasenaś ca nāmataḥ
english: They were named Kakṣasena, Ugrasena, the valiant Citrasena, Indrasena, Suṣeṇa, and Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: janamejayasya tanayā bhuvi khyātā mahābalāḥ dhṛtarāṣṭraḥ prathamajaḥ pāṇḍur bāhlīka eva ca
english: The mighty sons of Janamejaya, renowned on earth, were — Dhṛtarāṣṭra the firstborn, Pāṇḍu, and Bāhlīka.

sanskrit: niṣadhaś ca mahātejās tathā jāmbūnado balī kuṇḍodaraḥ padātiś ca vasātiś cāṣṭamaḥ smṛtaḥ sarve dharmārthakuśalāḥ sarve bhūtahite ratāḥ
english: Also Niṣadha of great splendor, the strong Jāmbūnada, Kuṇḍodara, Padāti, and Vasāti the eighth — all were skilled in dharma and artha, all devoted to the welfare of living beings.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭro 'tha rājāsīt tasya putro 'tha kuṇḍikaḥ hastī vitarkaḥ krāthaś ca kuṇḍalaś cāpi pañcamaḥ haviḥśravās tathendrābhaḥ sumanyuś cāparājitaḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra then became king; his sons were Kuṇḍika, Hastī, Vitarka, Krātha, Kuṇḍala the fifth, Haviḥśravā, Indrābha, Sumanyu, and Aparājita.

sanskrit: pratīpasya trayaḥ putrā jajñire bharatarṣabha devāpiḥ śaṃtanuś caiva bāhlīkaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: O bull of the Bharatas, three sons were born to Pratīpa: Devāpi, Śaṃtanu, and Bāhlīka the great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: devāpis tu pravavrāja teṣāṃ dharmaparīpsayā śaṃtanuś ca mahīṃ lebhe bāhlīkaś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Of them, Devāpi retired to the forest in pursuit of dharma; Śaṃtanu obtained the earth, and Bāhlīka became a great chariot-warrior.

sanskrit: bharatasyānvaye jātāḥ sattvavanto mahārathāḥ devarṣikalpā nṛpate bahavo rājasattamāḥ
english: Many best of kings were born in Bharata's lineage, O king — great chariot-warriors of powerful nature, comparable to divine sages.

sanskrit: evaṃvidhāś cāpy apare devakalpā mahārathāḥ jātā manor anvavāye ailavaṃśavivardhanāḥ
english: And likewise other great chariot-warriors comparable to gods were born in the lineage of Manu — those who augmented the Aila line.

sanskrit: janamejaya uvāca śrutas tvatto mayā vipra pūrveṣāṃ saṃbhavo mahān udārāś cāpi vaṃśe 'smin rājāno me pariśrutāḥ
english: Janamejaya said: O brahmin, I have heard from you the great origin of my ancestors, and I have now learned of the noble kings in this lineage.

sanskrit: kiṃ tu laghvarthasaṃyuktaṃ priyākhyānaṃ na mām ati prīṇāty ato bhavān bhūyo vistareṇa bravītu me
english: But the pleasant narrative, being too brief in content, does not fully satisfy me — so please tell me again in greater detail.

sanskrit: etām eva kathāṃ divyām ā prajāpatito manoḥ teṣām ājananaṃ puṇyaṃ kasya na prītim āvahet
english: This very divine story — the holy birth of those kings from Prajāpati down to Manu — whose heart would it not gladden?

sanskrit: saddharmaguṇamāhātmyair abhivardhitam uttamam viṣṭabhya lokāṃs trīn eṣāṃ yaśaḥ sphītam avasthitam
english: Their fame, swelled by the greatness of good dharma and virtue, stands exalted, pervading all three worlds.

sanskrit: guṇaprabhāvavīryaujaḥsattvotsāhavatām aham na tṛpyāmi kathāṃ śṛṇvann amṛtāsvādasaṃmitām
english: I am not sated hearing the tale of those endowed with virtue, splendor, valor, energy, strength, and zeal — a tale that tastes like nectar.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca śṛṇu rājan purā samyaṅ mayā dvaipāyanāc chrutam procyamānam idaṃ kṛtsnaṃ svavaṃśajananaṃ śubham
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Listen, O king — hear fully what was properly heard by me from Dvaipāyana long ago, this auspicious account of the entire origin of your own lineage being now recounted.

sanskrit: dakṣasyāditiḥ aditer vivasvān vivasvato manuḥ manor ilā ilāyāḥ purūravāḥ purūravasa āyuḥ āyuṣo nahuṣaḥ
english: From Dakṣa came Aditi; from Aditi came Vivasvat; from Vivasvat came Manu; from Manu came Ilā; from Ilā came Purūravas; from Purūravas came Āyu; from Āyu came Nahuṣa.

sanskrit: yayāter dve bhārye babhūvatuḥ uśanaso duhitā devayānī vṛṣaparvaṇaś ca duhitā śarmiṣṭhā nāma atrānuvaṃśo bhavati
english: Yayāti had two wives: Devayānī, daughter of Uśanas, and Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvā. Here the genealogical succession continues.

sanskrit: yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva devayānī vyajāyata druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī
english: Devayānī bore Yadu and Turvasu; Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvā, bore Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru.

sanskrit: tatra yador yādavāḥ pūroḥ pauravāḥ
english: Of these, the Yādavas descend from Yadu, and the Pauravas from Pūru.

sanskrit: pūror bhāryā kausalyā nāma tasyām asya jajñe janamejayo nāma yas trīn aśvamedhān ājahāra viśvajitā ceṣṭvā vanaṃ praviveśa
english: Pūru's wife was named Kausalyā; to her was born his son Janamejaya, who performed three Aśvamedha sacrifices and then, after performing the Viśvajit sacrifice, entered the forest.

sanskrit: janamejayaḥ khalv anantāṃ nāmopayeme mādhavīm tasyām asya jajñe prācinvān yaḥ prācīṃ diśaṃ jigāya yāvat sūryodayāt tatas tasya prācinvatvam
english: Janamejaya married Anantā, a Mādhavī princess; to her was born his son Prācinvān, who conquered the eastern direction as far as the sunrise — hence his name Prācinvān.

sanskrit: prācinvān khalv aśmakīm upayeme tasyām asya jajñe saṃyātiḥ
english: Prācinvān married a princess of the Aśmaka people; to her was born his son Saṃyāti.

sanskrit: saṃyātiḥ khalu dṛṣadvato duhitaraṃ varāṅgīṃ nāmopayeme tasyām asya jajñe ahaṃpātiḥ
english: Saṃyāti married a daughter of Dṛṣadvata named Varāṅgī; to her was born his son Ahaṃpāti.

sanskrit: ahaṃpātis tu khalu kṛtavīryaduhitaram upayeme bhānumatīṃ nāma tasyām asya jajñe sārvabhaumaḥ
english: Ahaṃpāti married a daughter of Kṛtavīrya named Bhānumatī; to her was born his son Sārvabhauma.

sanskrit: sārvabhaumaḥ khalu jitvājahāra kaikeyīṃ sunandāṃ nāma tasyām asya jajñe jayatsenaḥ
english: Sārvabhauma carried off by conquest a Kaikeyī princess named Sunandā; to her was born his son Jayatsena.

sanskrit: jayatsenaḥ khalu vaidarbhīm upayeme suṣuvāṃ nāma tasyām asya jajñe arācīnaḥ
english: Jayatsena married a Vidarbhā princess named Suṣuvā; to her was born his son Arācīna.

sanskrit: arācīno 'pi vaidarbhīm evāparām upayeme maryādāṃ nāma tasyām asya jajñe mahābhaumaḥ
english: Arācīna also married another Vidarbhā princess named Maryādā; to her was born his son Mahābhauma.

sanskrit: mahābhaumaḥ khalu prāsenajitīm upayeme suyajñāṃ nāma tasyām asya jajñe ayutanāyī yaḥ puruṣamedhānām ayutam ānayat tad asyāyutanāyitvam
english: Mahābhauma married a princess of Prasenajiṭ named Suyajñā; to her was born his son Ayutanāyī, who performed ten thousand Puruṣamedha sacrifices — hence his name Ayutanāyī.

sanskrit: ayutanāyī khalu pṛthuśravaso duhitaram upayeme bhāsāṃ nāma tasyām asya jajñe akrodhanaḥ
english: Ayutanāyī married a daughter of Pṛthuśravas named Bhāsā; to her was born his son Akrodhana.

sanskrit: akrodhanaḥ khalu kāliṅgīṃ karaṇḍuṃ nāmopayeme tasyām asya jajñe devātithiḥ
english: Akrodhana married a Kāliṅga princess named Karaṇḍu; to her was born his son Devātithi.

sanskrit: devātithiḥ khalu vaidehīm upayeme maryādāṃ nāma tasyām asya jajñe ṛcaḥ
english: Devātithi married a Videha princess named Maryādā; to her was born his son Ṛca.

sanskrit: ṛcaḥ khalv āṅgeyīm upayeme sudevāṃ nāma tasyāṃ putram ajanayad ṛkṣam
english: Ṛca married an Aṅga princess named Sudevā; to her he fathered a son named Ṛkṣa.

sanskrit: ṛkṣaḥ khalu takṣakaduhitaram upayeme jvālāṃ nāma tasyāṃ putraṃ matināraṃ nāmotpādayām āsa
english: Ṛkṣa married a daughter of Takṣaka named Jvālā; to her he gave birth to a son named Matināra.
